mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing present value.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases the risk-free rate and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly lower when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% compared to when it is <= 3.0% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 2.5%, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases the risk premium on equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 1 month AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL>2.5) does not produce negative returns in >60% of cases over 3 years, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), the S&P 500 tends to have positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is likely to implement monetary easing, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly higher when UNRATE > 5.5% compared to when it is <= 5.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A higher housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong housing activity signals robust economic demand, leading to higher corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: Rank IC between HOUST and 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic growth concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly lower when HOUST < 1000 compared to when it is >= 1000 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below 110 and housing starts (HOUST) is below 1000, it signals a simultaneous contraction in manufacturing and housing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced economic activity and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: The joint condition (INDPRO<110 AND HOUST<1000) does not produce negative returns in >60% of cases over 3 years, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 215), the S&P 500 tends to have negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly lower when CPIAUCSL > 215 compared to when it is <= 215 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.
